title: Give the gateway its own STANs on the upstream link

blocks.text: This is the gateway from 12.3.1, and it is lunchtime. Three hundred terminals send their purchases through `Upstream.forward`, and the host knows the gateway as a single terminal, `GW000001`. Some purchases fail with `Duplicate key`.
`forward` already works for one terminal. Finish the three methods marked `TODO` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Upstream.java` so that it also works for many:

items: `nextStan()`: the gateway's numbering for its own link;

blocks.text: The comment on each method says what it is for. When you're done, two terminals can send the same STAN at the same moment and both get their answers, and each terminal recognises the answer as its own. About ten lines in total.
The tests run a real QMUX against a test host like the one in 12.1. Some of them keep two purchases in flight at once.

cases.says: a terminal's purchase is relayed under the gateway's ID and the terminal gets the host's answer
the response a terminal receives carries the STAN the terminal sent, not the gateway's
the response a terminal receives carries the terminal's own ID, not the gateway's
two terminals that use the same STAN at the same moment both get their answers, because the gateway numbers its own link
two messages in flight on the link never share a STAN, so one sequence serves the whole link rather than one per terminal
the six-digit STAN wraps from 999999 to 000001 and is never 000000

origin.section: 12.3.1 Spot the Problem: The Gateway at Lunchtime

concepts: A response finds its request because both produce the same key; what differs between them (the response digit, the repeat digit) is left out.
Only one request per key can wait, so the sender of a link must number its own messages; per-terminal or relayed STANs collide.
